Such a theory has the great merit that it does away with the old dichotomy between 'matter*, represented by particles of one-half-integer spin, and 'interactions', represented by integer-spin particles. It also has the great advantage that many of the infinities that arise in quantum theory cancel each other out. paragraphs.source_en: Although we do not yet have a proper quantum theory of gravity, let alone one that unifies it with the other physical interactions, we do have an idea of some of the features it should have. One of these is connected with the fact that gravity affects the causal structure of space-time; that is, gravity determines which events can be casually related to one another. An example of this in the classical theory of general relativity is provided by a black hole, which is a region of space-time in which die gravitational field is so strong that any light or other signal is dragged back into the region and cannot escape to the outside world.
